title: BBQ Honey Chicken Protein Pizza (Justin cut)
creator: Justin adaptation (mild BBQ-honey, no spicy BBQ)
summary: Mild BBQ-honey chicken pizza with veggies on the high-protein low-carb crust. Sauce uses sugar-free BBQ plus Justin’s sweetener kit for a honey vibe — not spicy BBQ.
whyItFits: High protein: chicken + LC cottage-cheese dough + mozzarella
Lower carb / cal: almond-flour crust, sugar-free BBQ, 0-sugar sweetener
Sweetener kit shines here (monk fruit / stevia / 0-sugar syrup)

items: 2–3 tbsp sugar-free BBQ sauce (mild / original — avoid “chipotle,” “hot,” or “spicy” labels)
1/2–1 tsp 0-sugar simple syrup (sucralose) or a pinch of monk fruit / granulated stevia, to taste — honey vibe without sugar
Optional: tiny splash of apple cider vinegar or water to thin; pinch garlic powder
3–4 oz cooked chicken breast, shredded or cubed (tossed in a little of the BBQ-honey sauce)
Optional finish: chopped cilantro (mild herb note — skip if you don’t like it)

steps: Make and par-bake the LC dough per the dough recipe (425°F until set).
Stir sugar-free BBQ with 0-sugar syrup or monk fruit/stevia until it tastes mildly sweet-smoky (“honey BBQ” without heat). Adjust sweetener to taste.
Toss chicken in ~1 tbsp of the sauce. Spread remaining sauce thinly on the crust.
Add spinach if using, then chicken, onion, and bell pepper. Top with mozzarella.
Bake 8–12 minutes at 425°F until cheese melts and crust edges brown. Optional brief broil.
Rest 2 minutes. Optional cilantro. Slice and serve.
substitutions: Sweeteners: 0-sugar simple syrup (sucralose), monk fruit, or granulated stevia — any of the three for the honey vibe; start small and taste.
No spicy BBQ: use mild sugar-free BBQ only; skip cayenne, chipotle, and hot sauce.
Lower cal: thinner sauce layer, part-skim mozzarella, lean chicken breast.
Extra protein: more chicken; optional whey in the dough.
Veggies: onion + bell pepper are core; spinach optional; mushrooms fine if mild.
notes: The “honey” is all sweetener kit — no real honey needed for the macros cut.
If BBQ brand is already sweet, you may need little or no extra sweetener.
Pair with the same dough as Hawaiian so you can do one of each personal pizza from one batch.
Viral cottage cheese dough reels often use wheat flour; this pizza assumes the almond-flour Justin dough.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate for 1 personal pizza with half LC dough, chicken, sugar-free BBQ + sweetener, part-skim mozzarella, veggies. Not lab-tested.

title: Beef Chow Fun (Justin cut)
creator: YouTube Shorts (restaurant-style beef chow fun)
summary: Restaurant-style beef chow fun from a YouTube Short — wok-seared marinated flank, thick noodles, bean sprouts, and a savory soy-oyster sauce. Justin cut bumps the beef, skips white pepper heat, swaps sugar for the sweetener kit, and calls out a clear lower-carb noodle option.
whyItFits: High protein: more flank steak than the typical restaurant ratio
Mild — no chili oil, no white pepper kick
Sweetener kit replaces sugar in the sauce
Easy to lean lower-carb with protein noodles / konjac / half rice noodles

items: 12–14 oz (340–400 g) flank steak, thinly sliced against the grain (bump vs typical ~8 oz for protein)
2 green onions, whites and greens separated (whites for sauté, greens for finish)
1–2 tbsp neutral oil for the wok
1/2–1 tsp 0-sugar simple syrup or a pinch monk fruit / granulated stevia (in place of sugar)
Classic: 10–12 oz fresh thick rice noodles (hor fun / chow fun), loosened under warm water if refrigerated
Lower-carb Justin option (called out): protein noodles, shirataki/konjac “wide” noodles (rinsed + dried well), or half rice noodles + half konjac/protein noodles — same sauce and beef load

steps: Slice flank thin against the grain. Mix with soy, oyster, Shaoxing, baking soda, and cornstarch. Rest 15 minutes.
Mix the sauce (light soy, dark soy, oyster, Shaoxing, sesame oil, sweetener kit — no white pepper). Set aside.
Prep onion, garlic, ginger, green onion whites/greens, and bean sprouts. Loosen noodles so they’re ready to toss.
Heat a wok or large skillet until very hot. Add oil, sear beef in a single layer until just browned (don’t overcook). Remove to a plate.
Add a splash more oil if needed. Stir-fry onion + green onion whites a few minutes. Add garlic + ginger; cook ~30–60 seconds until fragrant.
Add noodles, seared beef, and sauce. Toss hard so noodles pick up color and sauce coats everything.
Add bean sprouts + green onion greens. One final toss (sprouts stay crisp). Serve hot.
substitutions: No spice / mild: omit white pepper and any chili oil; sesame oil + soy/oyster carry the flavor.
Sweeteners: monk fruit, stevia, or 0-sugar simple syrup instead of sugar — start small and taste.
More protein: 12–14 oz (or up to 1 lb) flank; don’t skimp the sear.
Lower carb: protein noodles, rinsed konjac/shirataki wide noodles, or a half-and-half of rice noodles + konjac — keep full beef amount.
Shaoxing: dry sherry or a splash of stock + tiny splash rice vinegar if you don’t keep Shaoxing.
Gluten-aware: use gluten-free tamari and check oyster sauce label.
notes: Source: https://youtu.be/R8AMIk2h3JE — restaurant-style beef chow fun Short (marinade 15 min; sear–veg–noodles–sauce–sprouts flow).
Hot wok + don’t crowd the beef = restaurant sear at home.
Fresh rice noodles clump when cold — loosen gently with warm water before the pan.
Baking soda in the marinade tenderizes; don’t skip for flank.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Midpoint estimate for Justin LC path (protein/konjac or half rice noodles) with ~13 oz flank total (~6.5 oz/serving). Classic rice noodles higher carb (~50–60g). Not lab-tested.

title: Crockpot Creamy Chicken Pasta (Justin cut)
creator: Cooking in the Midwest (Luke Brown)
summary: Viral crockpot dump dinner from Cooking in the Midwest — creamy tomato “pink sauce” chicken pasta. Adapted for no spice, higher protein, and lower carb/cal without losing the cozy pasta vibe.
whyItFits: Easy to lean protein-heavy with pasta swaps

items: 1.5–2 lb boneless skinless chicken breast (original uses 1 lb — bump this for your protein goals)
Skip the original 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes
24 oz jar lower-sugar marinara (Rao’s, Carbone, or similar no-added-sugar style)

15 oz jar light Alfredo or a lighter DIY: 3/4 cup plain nonfat Greek yogurt + 1/2 cup low-fat milk + 1/3 cup grated Parmesan + pinch garlic powder, whisked smooth (stir yogurt version in after cooking so it doesn’t split)
8–12 oz pasta (not a full 16 oz box) — prefer protein pasta (Barilla Protein+, chickpea, or high-fiber) or a half-and-half of regular cellentani + zucchini noodles
Optional: big handful fresh spinach when you add the mozzarella

steps: Spray the crockpot. Add chicken. Season with salt, pepper, onion powder, and Italian seasoning (no chili flakes). Add garlic.
Pour marinara and jar Alfredo over the top (if using Greek-yogurt Alfredo, use marinara only now and hold the yogurt sauce for step 5).
Cook on LOW 4–6 hours (or HIGH 3–4 hours) until chicken hits 165°F.
Remove chicken, cube or shred, return to the crock. Stir in mozzarella (and spinach if using). Keep on low/warm.
Boil pasta until just al dente; drain. Stir into the crock. If using yogurt Alfredo, whisk it in off heat or on warm only, then fold in pasta.
Top with Parmesan and parsley. Serve.
substitutions: No spice: omit red pepper flakes entirely; Italian seasoning + garlic + onion powder carry the flavor.
Lower carb: protein/chickpea pasta, or 6–8 oz pasta + spiralized zucchini; keep the full chicken amount.
Lower cal Alfredo: light jar, or Greek-yogurt + Parmesan “alfredo” stirred in at the end.
Lower-sugar marinara: pick a jar with no added sugar.
Sweeteners: not needed here — this dish isn’t sweet. Save stevia / monk fruit / 0-sugar syrup for teriyaki-style sauces later.
Extra protein: 2 lb chicken, part-skim mozzarella, protein pasta.
notes: Original reel caption: “Here’s an easy crockpot recipe for a busy weeknight dinner! #EasyRecipes #dinnerideas #crockpot”
Original often shows Bertolli Alfredo + Prego + cellentani — swap brands freely for macros.
Leftovers: reheat gently with a splash of milk or broth so the sauce stays creamy.
Stovetop shortcut: season and cook cubed chicken, add sauces, simmer, fold in cooked pasta + cheese.

nutritionPerServing.notes: Estimate for ~5 servings using 1.75 lb chicken breast, 10 oz Barilla Protein+ pasta, 24 oz lower-sugar marinara, light Alfredo (or Greek-yogurt DIY), part-skim mozzarella. Assumes drained pasta and sauce distributed evenly. Not lab-tested — label as estimate.
